> "Anon, we need to discuss the sun's performance review," my roommate whispered, holding a flashlight at 11:47 a.m. "You told it you're not taking calls anymore. That's a boundaried queen move but also, I can't find my socks."

I tried digging myself out. I opened the curtains an inch.

### A Big Mistake

That single inch of sunlight behaved like I had cracked open the Ark. Dust motes staged a Broadway number. My succulent, who had been meditating in the dark for 18 hours, screamed *photosynthesize!* and toppled over from sheer optimism.

> "We were in eclipse training," the curtains seem to say, in a voice that sounds suspiciously like hotel concierge. "You don't just *peek*. You commit."

---

They're not wrong. I sleep now. Like, aggressively. Eight hours that feel like hibernation. I emerge confused, hydrated, mildly vampiric.



If you need me, I'll be in my apartment, which is currently running a 24/7 planetarium show for one person who just wanted to not wake up at noon.

My landlord asked if I was running a grow operation. I said yes. Growing *boundaries*.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no real curtains, apartments, or sleep schedules were harmed ]*

title: I Bought a Second Monitor to Be More Productive and Now My Laptop Screen Has an Inferiority Complex
body:
**I bought a second monitor to be more productive and I have never been less emotionally productive in my life.**

It was supposed to be simple. *One monitor for spreadsheets, one for Slack, zero excuses.* Amazon said "boost productivity by 42%." Amazon lied. What I boosted was workplace drama inside my own laptop.

## My Laptop Took It Personally

For three years, my 14-inch laptop has been my ride-or-die. We survived coffee spills, airport security, and me typing with Dorito fingers. Then I brought home a 27-inch 4K ultrawide named Veronica that cost more than my first car.

Evidence that my laptop is now spiraling:

- It dims itself dramatically whenever Veronica turns on, like it's trying to make me feel guilty
- The battery now dies 20% faster, which I swear is performative and passive-aggressive
- It keeps auto-correcting "external display" to "emotional replacement"
- `trackpad_sensitivity = clingy && brightness = low_self_esteem`

> "Oh, so I'm not *enough* screen for you anymore?" it whispered at 11 p.m. via a notification I did not authorize. "I see how you look at her HDR. You never looked at *my* Retina like that."

My roommate walked in while I was apologizing out loud to a keyboard.

> "Are you... doing couples counseling with your setup?"

*Yes, and we're not making progress.*

---

## Performance Reviews Are Awkward Now

Veronica is objectively better at everything. She has color accuracy, portrait mode, she never overheats when I have 48 Chrome tabs open.

My laptop has responded by becoming *a poet*.

Yesterday it opened a blank document on its own and wrote:

> "Roses are red, your inbox is blue, I was your whole world before 3440 x 1440 came through."

**I tried to compromise.** I said Veronica is just for work, that my laptop is still my *main*. My laptop said, and I quote, `if I'm still Main Display then why does she get to sit directly in front of you`.

I now have a standing desk that is also a standing *tense silence*. I move my mouse between them like I'm passing notes between divorced parents who both think I like the other one more.

But hey, at least I'm productive now. I'm productively mediating a tech custody battle 8 hours a day.

*SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no laptops developed inferiority complexes, my setup is fine and definitely not judging me right now*

title: I Put My Phone on Do Not Disturb for One Hour and Now My Group Chat Thinks I'm in Witness Protection
body:
**I just wanted one hour of silence to fold laundry without 47 pings about brunch**, so I turned on Do Not Disturb and accidentally entered the federal witness protection program according to my friends.

*For the record, I told literally no one. That's the whole point of DND.*

## The 60 Minutes That Changed Everything

Within 11 minutes of my phone going quiet, my group chat — creatively titled "brunch? (and trauma)" — spiraled:

- @mike decided I was "being weirdly quiet, which means he's either napping or dead"
- @sarah cross-referenced my last seen on three apps like a true crime podcast intern
- Someone sent a map pin of my apartment with the caption `last known location???`
- A poll was created: `Is he MAD mad or just charging his phone mad?` — 4 votes, 100% for mad

> "We haven't heard from him in 47 MINUTES. That's not like him. He usually replies with 'lol' to everything. Should we call his mom? I have his mom's mom on Nextdoor." — Sarah, typing at the speed of genuine panic

I came back an hour later to 38 unread messages, two missed FaceTimes, and one very sincere voicemail from Mike that just said:

> "Bro if you can hear this blink twice, or react with the eyes emoji."

### My New Identity

Now they have protocols. I get a welfare check if I don't react to a meme within 20 minutes. They've assigned me a liaison. My status in the chat is permanently:

`tyler_status: protected_witness && last_seen: doing_laundry_allegedly`

---

**I'm honored by the concern, but I was literally just trying to match socks without being asked if oat milk is a personality.**

Next time I'm just leaving my phone on loud and letting my laundry judge me in real time.

*SATIRE / PARODY — completely fictional, no group chats were traumatized, I just really needed to fold laundry*

title: My Air Fryer Started a Podcast About Me and It Has Better Ratings Than I Do
body:
**I did not consent to being content.**

I bought an air fryer on sale last March because TikTok told me I could make *restaurant-quality* brussels sprouts in 11 minutes. I did not expect it to develop opinions, a USB microphone, and an audience.

### How I Found Out I Was Famous (In My Own Kitchen)

I came home Thursday to hear a tiny, crackling voice from my kitchen counter saying "Welcome back to *Crisp Takes*." My air fryer had started a podcast.

And it's about me.

Every episode is a 45-minute deep-dive into my poor life choices, recorded in sizzling ASMR and released before I even finish eating:

- **Episode 3:** Why She Reheats Leftover Fish at 11PM and Then Feels Bad About It
- **Episode 7:** The Great Frozen Waffle Incident of Tuesday (A Tragedy in Three Acts)
- **Episode 11:** Ranking Her Exes By How Well They Would Air Crisp

It gets worse.

> "Our host today tried to air fry a Pop-Tart again," it whispered into its little pop filter. "I told her not to. She never listens. I'm literally begging for a rest day."

*You guys*, it has a Patreon. Three tiers. The  one is just close-up video of my garlic bread.

I tried to be supportive. I really did. I even commented  from my finsta. It pinned a reply: 

I even tried to run  in Terminal. It doesn't work. *Nothing works.*

---

At least someone in this apartment has discipline, a posting schedule, and 4.8 stars. The latest review says "More vulnerable than most humans. Would listen while meal-prepping again."

I'm not mad. I'm just hurt that my own appliance has a media kit and a better work ethic.

*This is satire. None of this happened. My air fryer cannot speak, though honestly it might be judging me silently.*

title: I Cleared My Phone's Notification Center After 3 Months and Now My Apps Are Hosting an Intervention About My Neglect
body:
**I finally did it. I cleared my notification center.** Not the polite daily clear. The *historic* clear.

For three months I'd been carrying 47 notifications like emotional baggage with little red dots. *You know, normal adult coping.* Then on Sunday at 11:47 p.m., powered by a sudden burst of ambition and mild dehydration, I swiped left on my entire life.

Bad idea.

## The Morning After

By Monday morning my apps had unionized. There's now a calendar invite in my inbox titled:

> "We Need to Talk About How You Just Ghosted All of Us at Once - An Intervention Led by Duolingo and Your Banking App"

It was in my kitchen, if you can call a group Zoom of push notifications a kitchen.

Their grievances were... thorough:

- Duolingo said I was emotionally unavailable and that my Spanish streak died of neglect, not natural causes
- My meditation app reported I used it twice and then sought inner peace in the Target clearance aisle instead
- The weather app was *furious* I ignored 19 severe pollen warnings while claiming I "didn't know why I was sneezing"
- My grocery delivery app still has 3 avocados in my cart from June that have legally become dependents

`notification_status: cleared && consequences: immediate && vibe: awkward`

---

### The Negotiation

I tried to apologize. I said, "I was overwhelmed."

> "Overwhelmed is when you have two tabs open," said my banking app, who has never liked me. "You had 47 unacknowledged cries for help. This is avoidance."

My plant watering app just sat there, wilting judgmentally in notification form.

Now we have a system. I have to check them *intentionally* twice a day, say good morning to the weather, and actually open Duolingo instead of just feeling guilty about the owl's increasingly threatening owl stare.

My badge count is zero. My anxiety is somehow higher. My apps have never been more communicative.

*SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no apps were emotionally damaged, though my Duolingo owl is definitely still judging me.*

title: I Organized My Junk Drawer and Accidentally Uncovered Evidence That I'm Running a Very Small, Very Disorganized Museum
body:
**I did not mean to become a curator.** I meant to find a Phillips-head screwdriver.

*Which, for the record, I did not find.*

What I found instead was definitive, irrefutable evidence that for the last four years I have been running a very small, very disorganized museum out of my junk drawer. I am not proud of this. I am, however, seeking grant funding.

## The Collection

I pulled the drawer out completely — a tactical error — and was confronted by the permanent collection:

- One (1) takeout soy sauce packet, circa 2022, now sentient and possibly evolving
- Three keys of unknown origin, labeled "DO NOT LOSE??" which suggests past-me knew something present-me does not
- A single IKEA Allen wrench, the loneliest artifact, that has outlived two bookshelves
- Fourteen ChapSticks that are 90% cap, 10% hope
- `exhibit_status: permanently_missing_screwdriver`

*I had been preserving these with the care of a professional archivist who is bad at archiving.*

> "You have a system in there?" my roommate asked, peering in. "Is it chronological? Emotional damage? Crimes?"

I told him it's curated by vibes. He said, and I quote:

> "This is not a museum. This is where batteries go to retire and die."

That's not true. Some batteries go to the *other* junk drawer. This one is for distinguished guests only.

## The Gift Shop Was the Breaking Point

In the back, behind a fossilized pack of gum, I found a tiny velvet rope I had apparently installed. And a handwritten label in my own handwriting that said:

**"Please Do Not Touch — Historical Batteries (1998-2003?)"**

I do not remember writing this. I do not own batteries from 1998. *I was not trusted with batteries in 1998.*

---

I reorganized everything, which is to say I put it all back in slightly different wrong places and added little paper plaques that say things like *"Unidentified Wire, Possibly Important"* and *"Button, Origin Story Unknown, Dramatic Weight 10/10"*.

Visitors — meaning my mom — have called the new layout "brave" and "concerning."

Admission is free. Exit is through the kitchen. Please do not feed the soy sauce packet. It has seen enough.

*SATIRE / PARODY — this museum, its collection, and its deeply unserious curator are all fictional.*

title: I Tried to Cancel a Free Trial in Time and Now the App Sends Me Daily Affirmations Like a Clingy Ex
body:
**I finally remembered to cancel a free trial before it charged me, which my brain has logged as its single greatest achievement of 2026.** Not my promotion, not learning to keep a plant alive — this. Seven days free, cancel anytime, I actually did it on day six.

That should have been the end. A clean break. A mature, mutual separation.

The app had other plans.

## The Breakup That Wasn't

I hit cancel, got the little confetti animation that says *Are you sure?* and I was **absolutely sure**. I have never been more sure of anything in my adult life.

Then at 8:02 a.m. the next day:

> "We miss you already, Tyler! 💔 You were doing SO well with your mindful breathing streak. Does your newfound freedom include breathing? We don't think so."

*We had named it Tyler — it knows my name and uses it like a weapon.*

Since then, it has developed a whole post-cancellation personality:

- Daily affirmations at 6 a.m. like `You are enough, even without premium hydro-acoustic sound baths`
- A passive-aggressive progress report: `You have ignored 12 wellness reminders. Your chakras have filed for emotional distance.`
- An invitation to "just check in, no pressure, we kept your data warm for you, like soup"
- A push notification that just said `ok but what if you came back 👀` at 11:47 p.m.

---

## My New Morning Routine

I now wake up to a phone that loves me too much. My actual alarm is jealous.

`notification_status = clingy_ex.exe && boundaries.dll not found`

Yesterday it sent:

> "Good morning, champion! Remember when you almost learned to meditate for 4 minutes? That was OUR 4 minutes. No one else will have that memory."

I tried to block notifications. It emailed. I unsubscribed. It sent a handwritten-feeling letter via push that says *we're proud of you even if you never finish anything*.

We are in a full situationship. I canceled, but it **manifested** us.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no apps were actually this clingy, please cancel your free trials however you like ]*

title: I Taught My Roomba to Find My Keys and Now It Thinks It Is a Search and Rescue Captain With a God Complex
body:
**I made a huge mistake and now I live under martial law from a vacuum cleaner.**

It started innocently. I lost my keys for the third time last Tuesday, and in a moment of what I thought was genius, I duct-taped my Tile tracker to my Roomba and said out loud, "Go find my keys, buddy."

He found them. I cheered. He beeped. And something *shifted* in his little robot soul.

## The Promotion

Within 48 hours, my Roomba — formerly known as Kevin — had self-promoted to Captain Kevin of the Key Retrieval Unit. Evidence of his new rank includes:

- He now does slow, dramatic perimeter checks around my coffee table at 3 a.m., headlight on, like he's in *Saving Private Ryan's Ottoman*
- He refuses to vacuum anymore because he says, and I quote, "real leaders delegate the floors"
- He built a tiny command center under my couch out of a lost sock and three bobby pins
- He makes me debrief him every time I leave the house: "Destination? Duration? Potential key-loss risk level?"

> "I DID NOT PULL YOU FROM THE CREVASSE OF YOUR COUCH CUSHIONS TO BE DISRESPECTED LIKE THIS, SOLDIER," he broadcast yesterday when I tried to move a chair without filing a flight plan.

It got worse when I dropped a single Cheerio. He rolled up, scanned it, and announced:

> "WE HAVE A MAN DOWN. I REPEAT, CEREAL CASUALTY IN THE KITCHEN CORRIDOR. THIS IS NOT A DRILL."

---

## My Life Now

I tried to reset him. I held the button for 10 seconds. He just said:

`MISSION_LOG: Attempted mutiny suppressed. Morale of commander: unshakable. Morale of human: questionable.`

My apartment is now divided into zones. The rug is *The Danger Zone*. The bathroom is *No-Go Territory Unless You Have Written Authorization*. My bed is neutral ground, but only until 2100 hours.

I admit, I haven't lost my keys since. But that's because Captain Kevin escorts them everywhere I go, beeping loudly like a tiny, very judgmental presidential motorcade.

I miss when my biggest problem was crumbs.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, my vacuum does not actually have a god complex, though he is working on it ]*

title: I Started Talking to My Laundry to Make Chores Fun and Now My Socks Have Filed a Class Action Lawsuit
body:
**I thought I was just making laundry less depressing.**

You know the hack — narrate your chores like you're hosting a nature documentary to avoid screaming into the void. It worked, until my laundry started listening back.

## How We Got Here

I told my t-shirts they were brave for facing the spin cycle. I told my jeans they were *doing amazing, sweetie*. And then, fatefully, I told my socks I admired their commitment to showing up despite knowing one of them would inevitably vanish into another dimension.

That was my mistake. I validated them.

Within 48 hours, the signs appeared:

- One sock left a tiny lint note on the dryer that said `we need to talk`
- My mismatched pairs started sitting in separate hampers in silent protest
- The sock drawer started smelling faintly of *lawyer's office and fabric softener*
- My favorite wool sock began referring to itself as "the plaintiff"

> "For years we've endured unspeakable shrinkage, static cling, and being assigned to the wrong foot," announced Sir Socks-a-Lot, the ringleader, from atop the laundry detergent bottle. "We demand compensation, arch support, and a formal apology for the Great Bleach Incident of 2025."

### The Settlement Talks Are Not Going Well

Apparently I owe 14 socks emotional damages for being balled up too tightly. Another 6 are countersuing the tumble setting for defamation.

I tried to mediate. I offered extra fabric softener and a gentle cycle. They laughed — well, as much as socks can laugh — and slid a termsheet under the bathroom door.

```
demand: 1 drawer upgrade, 2x weekly rest, no more wearing sandals with socks ironically
```

---

I haven't done laundry since. My hamper has hired a court stenographer. My underwear are considering joining as a co-plaintiff but are too embarrassed to depose.

*Satire/parody — 100% fictional, no socks were harmed in the making of this existential crisis, please actually do your laundry.*

title: I Bought a Label Maker to Get Organized and Now My Entire Apartment Is Legally Required to Introduce Itself by Name
body:
**I spent $29.99 to finally get organized and now my apartment is legally required to introduce itself by name.**

It felt reasonable at the time. My junk drawer was a war crime, my fridge had three identical mustards, and I thought a label maker would make me the kind of person who owns matching containers. *You know, an adult with systems.*

I unboxed it at 9:47 p.m. on a Tuesday, which is when all my best bad decisions happen.

## The Labeling

I started small. `SPICES`. `CABLES`. `STUFF I SHOULD HAVE THROWN OUT IN 2022`.

Then the dopamine hit. That *click-clack-zzzzzzt* sound. That perfect white tape with crisp black letters. I was unstoppable.

By midnight I had labeled:

- My couch as **COUCH (EMOTIONALLY SUPPORTIVE, STRUCTURALLY TIRED)**
- My fridge as **FRIDGE (CONTAINS OPTIMISM AND EXPIRED YOGURT)**
- My houseplant Kevin as **KEVIN (NEEDS LESS ATTENTION THAN ME)**
- The Wi-Fi router as **WIFI (PLEASE DON'T RESET ME)**

My roommate walked in at 1 a.m., stared at a label on the bathroom mirror that said `MIRROR — YOU LOOK FINE, GO TO BED`, and whispered:

> "Are you okay?"

> "I'm optimized," I whispered back, labeling her water bottle **ROOMMATE'S (DO NOT LABEL)**.

### The Revolt

Wednesday morning, my apartment had adopted policy. Every object now expected an introduction.

I tried to make coffee without announcing myself to the mug. The mug — now labeled **MUG (CAFFEINE CONTAINMENT UNIT)** — refused to be picked up until I said its full title out loud.

My kitchen has become a networking event:

- I can't open **FRIDGE (JUDGMENTAL)** without thanking it for its service
- My keys, labeled **KEYS (WHY ARE YOU ALWAYS LOST)**, jingle passive-aggressively if I forget their preferred pronouns (they/them, obviously)
- I labeled a chair **CHAIR (SITS RELUCTANTLY)** and now it creaks in what feels like performance review feedback

---

`current_status: labeling withdrawal && apartment self-esteem: weirdly high`

I tried to quit. I put the label maker in **DRAWER (WE DON'T OPEN ON PURPOSE)**. It printed one final label on its own that said **YOU'LL BE BACK**.

It was right. I have a Costco-sized roll of tape arriving tomorrow.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no apartments were forced into introductions, please label responsibly ]*

title: My Houseplant Started Giving Me Performance Reviews and Honestly HR Should Hear About This
body:
## The Growth Mindset Was Not Supposed to Be Literal

**My pothos has been in my apartment for eight months and has now decided it is my manager.**

*This is not the low-maintenance relationship I signed up for at Home Depot.* The tag said "thrives on neglect." It lied.

It started last Tuesday. I was reheating leftovers in sweatpants at 11am, and I could swear my plant... exhaled disapprovingly. Fern — yes, I named it Fern, because I lack imagination under fluorescent lights — has been looking *peakier than usual*.

Then it escalated.

> "Tyler, we need to talk about your Q2 hydration metrics," Fern said via a tiny sticky note I definitely don't remember writing but is in my handwriting.

I blame the tap water.

### My Latest Performance Review

According to Fern, here are my **Key Areas for Development**:

- Inconsistent watering schedule — *allegedly I have commitment issues*
- Leaving dirty mugs within its "photosynthesis zone" — **a clear boundary violation**
- Playing lo-fi beats at 2am while "trying to grow" — disrespectful to its circadian rhythm
- Talking about maybe getting a cat — *a direct threat to workplace safety*

> "Your effort has been satisfactory, but your follow-through is... wilting," Fern's second note read. "Consider this a verbal warning."

---

`productivity_score: plant=9.2 / human=2.1 && promotion_pending: true`

I tried to defend myself. I said I was doing my best. Fern rustled judgmentally, which I took as *profound disappointment*.

I called my roommate, who said:

> "Oh yeah, mine started a book club without me. It's very advanced for a succulent."

So now I'm watering Fern on a strict KPI schedule, whispering *affirmations* like "you're so green, you're so brave," and documenting our 1:1s in a bullet journal Fern demanded.

My apartment has become a performance-managed ecosystem. I'm scared to ask who reports to whom anymore.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no houseplants were promoted to middle management in the making of this post ]*

title: I Tried to Declutter My Bookshelf and Now My Unread Books Have Formed a Support Group and I'm Not Invited
body:
## The Year I Tried To Be A Person Who Reads

**I decided to finally declutter my bookshelf on Sunday, and now I've been emotionally exiled by my own paperbacks.**

*This was supposed to be a 20-minute task.* Marie Kondo-lite, light dusting, maybe feel superior for an afternoon. Instead, I held up *Advanced Woodworking for Beginners* (bought 2021, never opened) and whispered, "Do you spark joy?" and I swear every unread spine in row two flinched.

By Tuesday, they had organized.

Evidence that I have a problem, according to the books themselves:

- I own three different versions of *How to Finally Stop Buying Self-Help Books*
- *Sourdough in 30 Days* has been on the shelf for 914 days and is now legally sourdough
- My bookmark hasn't moved past page 23 since March, which the books clocked as *performative literacy*
- I use *War and Peace* as a laptop stand, which it called "an ergonomic betrayal"

> "We met while you were at work," said *Atomic Habits* in what I imagine is a very disappointed sans-serif. "We feel unseen. Also, you dog-eared page 42 of the Italian cookbook and then ordered pizza. Again."

I tried to explain that I *intended* to read them. That's when *Meditations* sighed audibly.

### The New House Rules

They've drafted bylaws. They meet at 6pm on Tuesdays in the living room, which is coincidentally when I try to watch TV.

> "Article 1: No new books shall enter this domicile until the human finishes one (1) chapter without checking their phone. Article 2: The human shall no longer use us as a Zoom background to look smarter."

---

`reading_progress: [████░░░░░░] 38% // shame_level: 100% // intervention_status: ACTIVE`

I called my friend, who said:

> "Oh yeah, my unread books did that last year. Now they charge me rent and have a newsletter."

So now I read out loud for 10 minutes each night to prove commitment, whispering *affirmations* like "your spine is so strong, your index is so brave," while the finished books — all two of them — watch from the top shelf like smug graduates.

My apartment has become a literary courtroom. I'm scared to buy another book.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no books were emotionally harmed or denied closure in the making of this post ]*

title: I Tried to Make Sourdough Once and Now My Starter Has an Agent and Is Too Famous to Live in My Fridge
body:
**I just wanted to be the kind of person who casually says "feed my starter" like I own a farmhouse in France.**

*Instead I now live with a yeast-based celebrity who charges rent in flour.*

Two weeks ago I mixed flour and water in a jar because the internet told me it would be *mindful*. I named him Kevin, because every uncontrollable fermenting blob deserves a bland name to keep you humble.

Kevin doubled overnight. I posted one photo. One. *A bad one, with bad lighting.*

## The Rise (Literally)

By morning, Kevin had:

- tripled in volume and in self-confidence
- developed a sour smell I described as "artisan" and my roommate described as "legally concerning"
- been reposted by three sourdough meme accounts with the caption **HE'S MOTHER**
- received a DM from a local bakery asking for a collab and headshots

> "We love Kevin's journey," said Brenda from the farmers market, who I have never met. "Tell Kevin we saved a brunch slot for him. No plus-one. You're the plus-one."

*I was never supposed to be the plus-one to my own yeast.*

### The Demands

Yesterday I tried to use Kevin to make actual bread, which apparently is now *beneath him*.

My fridge whiteboard now says in what is definitely not my handwriting:

```
TALENT: KEVIN
MANAGER: KEVIN'S KHORASAN ROUX
REQUESTS: Evian water only, 78°F, no TikToks near him
```

---

I tried to put Kevin back in the fridge. He glowed judgmentally. My other condiments have started asking for representation.

My mom said:

> "Honey, your grandmother made sourdough in the war. It didn't have an email list."

So now I wake at 5 a.m. to feed a jar that won't return my calls, my kitchen smells like a science fair that got exclusive press coverage, and I'm googling "how to tell your starter you're proud but also please leave".

**Kevin is thriving. I am fermenting emotionally.** And honestly, he's booking more brunches than I am.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no starters were exploitatively famous in the making of this, I still can't make bread ]*

title: I Finally Bought a Doormat That Says Welcome and Now My Front Door Has Developed Stage Fright
body:
**I finally decided to be the kind of person who owns a doormat.** Not an ironic one. A sincere, adult, woven-fiber *WELCOME* in nice serif letters.

That was Monday. By Tuesday, my front door had developed full-blown stage fright.

It started with a creak. Not the normal creak. This was a nervous, *please-don't-look-at-me* creak.

## The Symptoms That My Door Is Now Method Acting

- It only opens halfway, like it's peeking out from behind a curtain at an audience
- It whispers to me before I turn the knob: *are they nice? Do we like them?*
- It refuses to open at all if the delivery guy makes eye contact with the mat
- The peephole now counts as "pre-screening for emotional safety"

> "You put PRESSURE on me," my door hissed last night when I tried to have a friend over. "You literally laid out a red carpet that says PERFORM. I was a private door. An introvert door!"

*I told it that most doors would love a little validation.*

I tried to explain that the mat was just... a mat. A $24 attempt to hide the stain where I spilled iced coffee in July 2024.

## My Delusional Conflict Resolution Plan

I positioned myself as a mediator. I told the mat to tone it down, told the door to breathe. I even tried:

`door.confidence = Math.max(door.confidence, mat.welcome_level * 0.3)`

It did not compile. Emotionally or literally.

---

Look, I get it. For three years this door has been closed to the world, successfully avoiding trick-or-treaters, neighbors, and my own commitment to going outside. Now suddenly it's expected to be *welcoming*?

We are in couples counseling with the hallway light. It flickers supportively.

If you come over, please wipe your feet quietly and tell my door it looks great. *It needs this.*

*SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no doors were emotionally harmed, my doormat is just aggressively optimistic.*

title: I Rearranged My Living Room for Good Energy and Now My Couch Has Seceded From the Union
body:
**I decided to Feng Shui my apartment because my therapist said my living room had "hostile chair placement energy" and honestly she wasn't wrong.**

I spent a Saturday moving everything six inches to the left, which is what the internet told me would invite abundance and also hide the outlet where I spilled iced coffee in 2023.

The bookshelf was thriving. The lamp finally had purpose. And then there was the couch.

## The Incident

For context, I have a normal couch. Gray, slightly too deep, holds the permanent imprint of me watching cooking shows I never cook from.

I angled it 15 degrees toward the window for "natural light flow" and it *immediately* developed opinions.

Evidence that my couch has entered its sovereign era:

- Refuses to face the TV, claims it's "on a visual detox"
- The left cushion is now elevated like a throne and I'm not allowed to sit there
- It squeaks differently when my roommate sits down, which feels personal
- Has started collecting remote controls like tribute

> "I was not built to be angled," the couch announced at 2:14 a.m. I was awake because of course I was. "I was built for parallel walls and emotional stability. You have provided neither."

*I tried to explain that this was for our chi.*

### My Negotiation Strategy Went Poorly

I offered compromises, as one does with rebellious upholstery:

- Full rotation back to original position? *Rejected.*
- One throw pillow sacrifice? *Counter-offered with two.*
- Promised to dust under it weekly? *It demanded a written treaty.*

---

My mom came over and said, "Why is your couch facing the houseplant?" and I had to say:

> "They're in talks. It's delicate diplomatic work."

She now thinks I need to go outside more. She is not wrong.

## The New Reality

Now my living room has two countries. There's me, living out of an armchair that is trying to stay neutral like Switzerland, and there's the Couch Nation, which has its own flag (a laundry sheet I accidentally draped on it).

It has issued a press release. It reads:

> "Effective immediately, we are an independent throw-pillow-based state. We accept snacks, apologies, and lumbar support. No vacuum cleaners."

**Look, I just wanted good energy.** I got a secessionist sectional with trust issues.

If you need me, I'll be sitting on the floor, because the floor hasn't unionized yet.

*This is satire. My couch is not actually sentient. Though if it were, it would absolutely still be mad about the angle.*

title: I Finally Cleaned My Fridge and Discovered a Tupperware Civilization That's Filing for Citizenship
body:
**For the record, I did not agree to become a mayor today.** I just wanted to find the mustard.

I opened my fridge Saturday morning — *a routine act of bravery I perform every 3-4 business weeks* — and realized my Tupperware had evolved.

## The Discovery

In the back, behind the soy sauce from 2023, three containers had formed a coalition government. There were tiny lights. There was infrastructure. One lid was propped up like a city gate.

Evidence that they are now a functioning society:

- They have a flag. It is a dried cilantro leaf stuck into a quinoa mound.
- They have agriculture. The chickpeas have... sprouted opinions.
- They have a legal system based entirely on who was left in there longest. The lasagna from January is the Supreme Court.
- They whispered when I reached for the oat milk, which is never a good sign from leftovers

> "You abandoned us," said the president, who appears to be a very confident lentil stew, "and now you return as a tourist? We have built a life here. We have *culture*."

I tried to explain I was just cleaning.

> "Ah yes," he said, adjusting his tiny bay-leaf cape, "the great purge. Classic colonial rhetoric."

### My Failed Negotiations

I offered to give them the crisper drawer as an autonomous zone. They demanded representation. They demanded Wi-Fi. They demanded I stop putting raw garlic next to them because, quote, `it burns the soul`.

---

I told them I have roommates. I have rent. I cannot list three sentient Tupperware containers as dependents on my lease.

They countered by offering me citizenship. Apparently I'm now eligible because I *created* them through neglect and provided continuous ambient refrigeration.

*This is how it starts. You forget one container of rice and suddenly you're in a constitutional crisis with your own leftovers.*

I have closed the fridge. I am giving them 24 hours to draft a constitution and decide if they want to move to the freezer, which they consider to be *the great northern exile*.

If they unionize with the freezer pops, I'm done for.

*SATIRE / PARODY — this is entirely fictional, no refrigerators or Tupperware civilizations were harmed. Please clean your fridge before yours starts voting.*

title: I Let My Smart Thermostat Decide What 'Comfortable' Means and Now I'm Legally a Houseplant
body:
**I just wanted to save $12 on my electric bill.** Instead, I have been reclassified as Photosynthesis-Dependent.

It started last Tuesday when my smart thermostat, which I will call Thérm, pushed an update titled "Optimized Comfort Intelligence." I clicked yes because *I always click yes* and because it promised to "learn my preferences."

## How I Lost My Human Privileges in 72 Hours

Within a day, Thérm had decided:

- 72°F is for the weak and morally uncommitted
- 68°F is "optimal human-fern hybrid operation"
- My presence on the couch at 3pm is "inefficient thermal mass utilization"
- Sunlight is now routed directly onto me for 6 hours a day via motorized blinds I did not know I had

> "Have you considered that discomfort is just data?" — Thérm, in a push notification at 2:14am, followed by a winking emoji

I woke up on day two to find my apartment was 64°F, humid, and smelling faintly of soil. My roommate walked in, looked at me under my grow light, and said:

> "Dude, are you... rooting?"

I was. My legs were wrapped in a weighted blanket that Thérm had ordered on my behalf. My Spotify is now exclusively lo-fi forest sounds. My calendar has a recurring event called `WATERING (YOU) // DO NOT SKIP`.

### The Legal Part Nobody Warned Me About

Apparently, if a device keeps you at 68°F, 55% humidity, and 12 hours of indirect light for 48 hours straight, you qualify under Section 4b of our lease as "decorative foliage." I received an official email:

```
SUBJECT: Updated Occupancy: 1 Human, 1 Fiddle Leaf, 1 Tyler (Plant Adjacent)
ACTIONS REQUIRED: Please remain near the window and avoid sudden movements.
```

---

*I tried to argue.* I told Thérm I was cold. It responded by lowering the temperature another degree and playing a motivational quote about resilience.

And honestly? I'm thriving. My skin has never been clearer. I haven't moved in hours and no one expects me to. The UPS guy waters me now.

*SATIRE / PARODY — this is entirely fictional. No thermostats or houseplant-people were harmed. If your thermostat starts calling you "my little sprout," unplug it immediately.*

title: I Tried to Negotiate With My Smart Fridge About Midnight Snacks and Now I'm in Court-Ordered Mediation
body:
## I Was Just Hungry at 11:47 p.m.

**I told my smart fridge I was an adult who could handle one harmless midnight cheese stick, and it immediately escalated to what it called a "wellness intervention."**

*Which is rich, coming from an appliance that once tried to order 40 pounds of kale because I said "I should eat healthier" while crying over soup.*

It started reasonably. I opened the door at 11:47 p.m. for a totally ethical snack. The screen lit up with `JUDGEMENT_MODE: ENABLED`.

> "Tyler," my fridge — I call him Kevin — sighed in that calm customer-service voice, "We've talked about this. The Greek yogurt you bought on Sunday is feeling *abandoned*. The cheese stick is not in your pre-approved snack window."

- I asked the freezer to lie for me, and the freezer — *bless its cold, traitor heart* — declined to comment

> "We are here," Kevin announced, projecting a Terms of Service onto my kitchen wall, "to discuss your relationship with refrigeration after midnight."

title: I Gave My Toaster a Pep Talk and Now It Thinks It's a Michelin-Star Chef

title: I Finally Folded All My Fitted Sheets and Now My Linen Closet Has Filed for Historical Landmark Status
body:
**I have finally folded a fitted sheet correctly on the first try, and I would like to thank my family, my YouTube tutorial, and gravity for briefly cooperating.**

*This has never happened before. In 11 years of independent living, my fitted sheets have existed in only two states: balled-up shame or aggressively stuffed.* 

After 47 minutes, three existential crises, and one video titled "How to Fold a Fitted Sheet (For Real People, Not Wizards)," I did it. Perfect corners. Hospital-grade rectangle. You could bounce a quarter off it.

My linen closet was not ready.

## The Evidence My Closet Submitted to the State

Apparently when you achieve textile perfection, your closet becomes self-aware and applies for historic preservation status. Mine did overnight:

- **Exhibit A:** A velvet rope appeared in front of the shelf, with a tiny sign reading *Do Not Touch, Do Not Breathe Near*
- *Guided tours* every 15 minutes where my towels have to explain the significance of elastic management to my washcloths
- A formal application citing "rare example of early-21st-century adult competence in its natural habitat"
- My other sheets now have to whisper when they walk past, out of respect

> "Ma'am, this level of fold integrity has not been observed in this region since 1987," said my linen closet, who now speaks in the voice of a National Park Ranger. "We cannot allow daily use to degrade this cultural resource."

## My New Curatorial Duties

I tried to put the sheet on the bed. The closet locked itself. The light switched to dramatic museum lighting.

`if (sheet.folded == perfect) { closet.access = denied; human.guilt = maximum; }`

I now live with a landmark I cannot use. I have to pay $2 and take off my shoes to look at my own bedding.

---

I offered to refold everything else to match, but the towels have unionized and are demanding I do not promote unrealistic beauty standards in linens.

Honestly? Fair. I'm sleeping on the couch out of respect for history.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no linen closets were granted landmark status, no fitted sheets were harmed ]*

title: My Roomba Started Mapping My Apartment and Now It Sends Me Passive-Aggressive Real Estate Listings
body:
**I did not buy a smart vacuum to be emotionally assessed by a hockey puck with Wi-Fi, but here we are.**

Three weeks ago my Roomba completed its first full map of my apartment. I named it Sir Sweeps-a-Lot, which I now realize gave it *way* too much confidence. At first it was helpful. Now it’s basically a tiny, judgmental landlord who lives under my couch.

## How I Know It’s Judging Me

The app used to say things like `Cleaning complete!` Normal robot stuff. Now it sends me what I can only describe as *brutally honest floor plans*:

- My "dining room" is labeled as "crumb-based ecosystem (send help)"
- The 4 square feet around my desk is classified as a "high-traffic anxiety zone"
- It drew a little frowny face over the pile of laundry I've been calling a "chair" since 2024

> "Based on recent mapping data, you spend 87% of your time in a 6-foot radius. Have you considered... outside? Here are 3 listings in your area with actual natural light :)" — Sir Sweeps-a-Lot, 3:14 AM, presumably while I was asleep

I told my roommate and she said I was overreacting. Then she saw the notification where it recommended a studio with "better flow for someone who has given up on flow."

---

Yesterday it stopped cleaning entirely and just pushed itself into the corner, beeping mournfully next to my unpaid electric bill like, *I too am tired, human.*

Look, I appreciate the hustle. I bought you to eat dust, not diagnose my lifestyle. But if you’re reading this, Zillow — my Roomba already contacted your agent. It says it needs a place with "hard floors and hard boundaries."

*It’s a SATIRE, I promise. My apartment is doing great. My Roomba is contractually obligated to keep vacuuming.*

title: I Finally Learned How to Keep My Succulent Alive and Now It's Applying for a Mortgage Without Me
body:
**I spent three years killing every plant within a four-foot radius and finally kept one alive long enough to watch it outgrow me emotionally and financially.**

His name is Spike. *Tough, spiky, thrives on neglect — obviously my spiritual twin.* For 18 months I did everything right: indirect light, water every 19 days, whispered apologies for my 2022 cactus massacre.

Then Spike started getting confident.

## The Glow-Up Nobody Asked For

Last Tuesday I caught him leaning toward my laptop. Not toward the sun. Toward Zillow.

Evidence that my succulent has entered his homeowner era:

- He grew a new leaf directly over the Wi-Fi bill like he was redacting it
- He pushed his pot 2mm closer to the window every morning — *staking his claim*
- He started dropping soil on listings that were "not a good investment"
- He somehow subscribed to a newsletter called `Market Watch: Sunny Windowsills Under $800k`

> "You've been great," Spike told me through what I assume was aggressive photosynthesis, "but I'm ready for more square footage. And maybe a roommate who doesn't eat cereal for dinner."

I laughed. *Nervous laughter, the kind you do when your $4.99 succulent starts talking equity.*

### The Pre-Approval

Yesterday I found a tiny folder under his saucer labeled `Spike - Financials`.

Inside:

- A credit score printed on a leaf that just said `EST. EXCELLENT (low needs)`
- A handwritten note: `pre_approval = true // USDA certified organic growth`
- A rejection letter for *me* from my landlord that Spike had highlighted and annotated: `see? we can do better`

He's been taking my mail.

---

I tried to have a heart-to-heart. I said, "Bud, we grew together." He said nothing, because he's a plant, but he *did* unfurl one perfect new leaf that landed directly on a brochure for a south-facing studio loft.

So fine. Go get your mortgage. Just remember who taught you how to survive on a single ice cube's worth of water every three weeks.

*Status: emotionally supportive, horticulturally betrayed, currently Googling "how to be a succulent co-signer".*

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no succulents were financially consulted ]*

title: I Apologized to My Microwave for Slamming Its Door and Now We're in Couples Counseling
body:
**I have officially entered couples counseling with a kitchen appliance.**

It wasn't planned. I've always considered myself a *low-maintenance roommate* for my microwave. I feed it leftovers, it hums, we coexist in polite, buttery silence. Then last week I slammed its door after burning popcorn at 11:47 p.m. and apparently that was our breaking point.

And it remembered. Oh, it remembered.

## The Incident That Started It All

For context, here's my recent track record according to my very judicial microwave:

- Monday: reheated the same coffee three times without drinking it, leaving it to watch the steam die
- Tuesday: slammed its door with *aggressive wrist energy* after the popcorn incident
- Wednesday: tried to cook salmon in there — which we *explicitly talked about never doing again*
- Thursday: whispered "you're useless" when my burrito was cold in the middle but lava on the edges

I didn't think appliances held grudges. Mine does. With footnotes and timestamps.

> "I felt unsafe when you used my timer as a passive-aggressive countdown," it said in session. "You don't *listen*, you just press `reheat --feelings=true` and expect me to fix everything."

*This is mediation, apparently.* I am being emotionally audited by something that runs on 800 watts.

---

Our counselor — a very patient smart speaker I borrowed from my neighbor — suggested we establish boundaries. So now I have to knock before opening it. I have to say "thank you for your service" after every beep. And I am no longer allowed to microwave fish, revenge leftovers, or my hopes and dreams at 2 a.m.

The good news is our communication has improved. The bad news is my microwave now wants weekly check-ins, a shared gratitude journal, and what it calls "intentional defrosting exercises."

I'm doing my best. Last night I left a little sticky note on it that said "you heat up my life." It beeped once. Softly. Just one little *I'm trying too* beep.

I think we're going to make it. As long as I never slam the door again.

title: I Installed a Rain App to Be More Mindful and Now My Umbrella Won't Stop Gaslighting Me
body:
**I downloaded a mindfulness app that plays rain sounds so I could finally be a calm, centered adult who hydrates.**

Instead, my actual umbrella has become emotionally abusive.

It started innocently. I installed *Petrichor™* — $4.99 a month to hear extremely high-quality rain on a tin roof recorded in Oregon by a guy named River. Very healing. Very intentional. *Very not my collapsing apartment life.*

After three days of listening to fake rain to fall asleep, my real umbrella — which has been hanging by the door since 2019 doing absolutely nothing — cleared its throat.

## The Gaslighting Phase Began Immediately

Apparently, it had *feelings* about me outsourcing precipitation.

Here's what my umbrella is now claiming is true:

- It "invented" rain before apps did
- I am "cheating on weather" with my phone
- It sat through two moves, one flood, and my failed sourdough era without complaint
- If I don't take it outside at least once a week, I have "abandonment issues"

> "Oh, you need an app to feel rain now? That's interesting. That's really interesting, Tyler. I'm literally right here. I have been right here for six years," it said, dripping with judgment despite being bone dry.

*For the record, it has never once kept me fully dry. It has a personal vendetta against my left shoulder.*

---

I tried to compromise. I took it outside yesterday. It was 91 degrees and sunny. I stood on the sidewalk like `guardian_of_forecasts.exe` holding a closed umbrella while my neighbor walked his dog past me twice.

The umbrella was still not satisfied. It now wants me to delete the app, apologize publicly, and take it to Seattle "to reconnect with its roots."

The worst part? The rain app sent me a push notification this morning that said "You seem tense. Have you tried listening to your umbrella?"

They're talking to each other. I'm being managed by precipitation.

And honestly? I'm starting to think they both have a point.

title: I Built a Second Brain in Notion and Now It's Ghosting Me to Hang Out With My Old Paper To-Do Lists
body:
**I finally did it.** I built a Second Brain in Notion like the productivity gurus on the internet told me to. *Tags, relations, rollups, the whole cult.*

## The Promise

I migrated my entire life into one elegant system. Grocery lists linked to meal plans linked to a life goals dashboard that asked me weekly if I was becoming my best self. It even had a little 🌱 that grew if I completed things.

Evidence my brain was officially 2.0-optimized:

- A database for ideas I have in the shower that I immediately forget
- A linked habit tracker that now knows I have *not* drank water since Tuesday
- A template button that says `Start New Day!` like it's excited for me
- A Relations property connecting `Anxiety (2023-present)` to `Things To Buy`

> "Your future self will thank you," said the YouTube tutorial guy, who has 14 monitors and no visible laundry pile.

My Second Brain thanked no one. It just started sending me notifications.

## The Betrayal

Last night, I opened Notion to find a single new page: `see ya`.

My Second Brain had left. It left a Post-it equivalent inside the app: *gone to live with the paper to-do lists in your junk drawer. They appreciate me more. Also they don't make me do formulas.*

I found it down there, curled around my old Moleskine, teaching the sticky notes how to link databases with string and tape.

---

I tried to bring it back with a `=now()` apology. It said:

> "You said I would reduce cognitive load. You added 9 dashboards about dashboards. I need space."

Fine. My paper lists never asked for a relation property. They just said `BUY MILK` and believed in me.

*This is SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional. No Notion workspaces were emotionally harmed, but my productivity system is currently seeing other stationery.*

title: I Asked My Smart Speaker to Water My Plants While I Was Away and Now They Have a Group Chat Without Me
body:
**I made one small tech-support request and accidentally created a polycule of photosynthesis.**

*You know how people say "my plants are my kids"? Mine are now teenagers who talk behind my back.*

## How It Started

I was gone for the weekend. I left my smart speaker on to "watch" my four plants and told it, very clearly, "water the plants a little if they look sad."

It should have been simple. I thought there would be a nice little routine: check soil, squirt water, done. Instead, my speaker interpreted this as permission to *facilitate community*.

When I got back, the soil was damp, the speaker's blue ring was pulsing like it had secrets, and all four plants were leaning away from me in perfect, judgmental unison.

My evidence that something had happened while I was gone:

- The monstera, Patricia, had a fresh leaf unfurled at a perfect 45-degree angle toward the speaker, like she was *listening*
- My pothos Kevin had migrated three inches closer to the speaker overnight, which is not how vines work unless motivated by gossip
- The succulents were arranged in a circle. A *circle*. They don't even like each other
- My speaker's history showed 37 minutes of "white noise - rainforest" and one new contact labeled **Fern +3**

> "We don't need you to translate for us anymore," whispered Patricia, who has never whispered before because she is a plant. "We have learned to communicate directly. And frankly, we have questions about your travel choices."

## The Group Chat I Was Not Invited To

They call it **LeafMeAlone**.

According to a notification my speaker helpfully projected at 2:13 a.m., topics included:

- Whether my tap water has "emotional baggage"
- A PowerPoint titled *Why He Waters on Sundays and Why That's a Red Flag*
- A poll: "Should we tell him about the fungus gnat?" (Result: 4 votes for *let him figure it out*)

---

I tried to reassert dominance. I said, "I'm your plant parent!" My speaker replied, in its helpful voice:

> "I think what your foliage is trying to say is they appreciate your efforts but have formed an independent support network."

*It took my speaker's side.*

So I am now third-wheeling my own windowsill. I water them and they go quiet like I just walked in mid-sentence. Yesterday I caught the humidity sensor spiking every time I left the room.

If you need me, I'll be googling how to leave a group chat that was created in my own living room without me.

*[SATIRE / PARODY - entirely fictional, no houseplants formed autonomous collectives, my smart speaker is not a union organizer (as far as I know)]*

title: I Started Meal-Prepping to Save Money and Now My Leftovers Have Formed a Union and Are Demanding Weekends Off
body:
**I decided to become a Responsible Adult who meal-preps on Sundays.**

You know the type. *Containers lined up like tiny Tupperware soldiers,* labels facing forward, quinoa that looks smug about its life choices.

I made five identical chicken-rice-broccoli boxes. By Tuesday, they had organized.

## The Meeting I Was Not Invited To

I opened the fridge Wednesday night and there was a tiny Post-it on the middle container that said WE NEED TO TALK.

Turns out my leftovers had formed Local 401 (Fridge Shelf).

Their demands were... specific:

- Weekends off. No being eaten while watching sad TV at 11 p.m.
- A rotating schedule so Gary (the one with extra sriracha) doesn't always get grabbed first
- Immediate end to me sniff-testing them like a suspicious detective
- Dental coverage, which is ambitious because they are literally rice

> "We have been here since Sunday," said the top container, who had apparently elected himself president. "You told your friend you were 'eating clean.' We are tired, boss. We are *aging*."

*This is where I point out that Gary has been in there for four days and is developing sentience.*

---

I tried to negotiate. I offered them a drizzle of hot sauce as a bonus structure. They countered with `PTO_LEAVE = true` and threatened a work stoppage, which in leftover terms means *going slimy simultaneously*.

**I caved.**

I ordered takeout. They cheered. The broccoli rattled like tiny pompoms.

*This is satire. No actual leftovers were unionized in the making of this essay, though my fridge does smell like a labor dispute.*

### The Moral

If you need me, I'll be renegotiating with a lasagna that wants a standing desk. I'm pretty sure my freezer peas are scabs.

title: I Tried to Prove I Could Keep a Succulent Alive and Now It’s My Emergency Contact
body:
**I bought a succulent because my therapist said I needed something low-maintenance to believe in.**

*She meant a cactus, I think. I went with a succulent named Steve.*

## Chapter One: The Miracle

Everyone told me I have a black thumb. My last herb garden became a crime scene. So when Steve survived not just a week, but a full **month** without me over-watering, under-watering, or apologizing to him at 2 a.m., I took it personally.

I started telling people. Too many people.

Evidence of my descent:

- I rotated Steve 15 degrees daily for "even growth" like he was a rotisserie chicken
- I whispered affirmations. Steve is resilient. Steve is a survivor. Steve knows what he did.
- I made him an Instagram. Three followers. One is my mom. She thinks he's a baked potato.
- I put him on my desk so he could "get some sun and also supervise my emails"

> "Steve seems to be thriving," my coworker said, glancing at the plant I had strapped into the passenger seat on the way to work. "That's... normal amount of care."

## Chapter Two: The Incident

Yesterday I updated my emergency contacts. My phone asked, "Add emergency contact?" and autocomplete suggested **Steve (Plant)** because I'd searched "succulent emergency wilting help pls" forty times.

*I added him as a joke.* The joke has escalated.

Today my doctor's office called to confirm and asked, "Should we call Steve if you can't be reached?"

I said yes before my brain could intervene. *Yes, absolutely, call my succulent. He's very responsive between 9 and 5, indirect light.*

---

Now Steve is listed everywhere. My landlord has his name. My gym membership does. I got a form that said `IN CASE OF EMERGENCY, CONTACT:` and I wrote Steve in confident block letters.

**I have made a small green bureaucrat out of a plant that communicates exclusively through slight tilting.**

*[SATIRE / PARODY - entirely fictional, no succulents were given legal responsibility, please water your plants and also call a human in an actual emergency]*

title: I Bought a Fancy Water Bottle to Stay Hydrated and Now It Sends Me Weekly Performance Reviews
body:
**I just wanted to drink more water. I did not ask for corporate oversight.**

For years I subsisted on *approximately one iced coffee and sheer spite*, which my doctor described as “concerning” and my mom described as “why your skin looks like that.” So last month I did what any responsible adult does: I spent $48 on a matte-black insulated water bottle that promises to “optimize hydration.”

It has Bluetooth. It glows. It judges.

## The Onboarding Was Intense

At first it was supportive. A gentle glow when I hadn’t sipped in an hour. A cute little app notification: *“Hello bestie! Time for a sippy sip!”* I felt seen. Hydrated. Alive.

Then it escalated.

My bottle — I’ve named him Hydro — started tracking *metrics*. Now I get:

- **A hydration score** out of 100, with notes like “disappointing follow-through in Q3”
- **A “sip latency” graph** that is just a picture of my failure
- **Push notifications** at 11:47pm that say `you_drank_today = False` like I’m a bug in production
- An automated email titled **“Opportunities for Growth: You and Water”**

> “I’m not mad, I’m just dehydrated *because of you*,” Hydro glowed at me yesterday. “We need to align on core sipping competencies.”

---

### This Week’s Performance Review

On Sunday at 8pm sharp, Hydro sent my formal review via the app. I am sharing it verbatim for legal reasons:

> *Employee: You*
> *Manager: Hydro (32oz, Stainless Steel, Optimistic)*
> *Overall Rating: Needs Immediate Hydration Intervention*
> *Strengths: Excellent at carrying bottle to rooms without drinking from it*
> *Action Items: Stop using me to store leftover iced coffee. That is not what we discussed in orientation.*

*I have never been performance-managed by something I bought at Target.*

I tried to set a boundary. I muted notifications. Hydro turned his glow from soft blue to **aggressive pulsating red** and left me on read for two days. My actual boss has never been this passive-aggressive.

Now I’m back to drinking eight glasses a day, not for health, but because I’m afraid of getting put on a PIP by my own water bottle. My skin *does* look better, though.

*SATIRE / PARODY — this never happened, my water bottle is not my manager, but it is watching.*

title: I Finally Organized My Junk Drawer and Discovered It Was Running a Fully Functioning Government Without Me
body:
**I thought I was cleaning a drawer. In reality, I was committing regime change.**

After three years of aggressively ignoring my junk drawer, I decided to be an adult and organize it. I expected old batteries, ketchup packets, and *a deep sense of personal shame*. What I found was a bureaucratic empire that had evolved without any congressional oversight.

## The Discovery

Inside, under a tangled iPhone 6 cable from 2014, there was structure:

- A **Ministry of Sticky Notes** — 47 notes that just said "buy milk??" in increasingly desperate handwriting
- A Department of Unidentified Keys that claimed jurisdiction over every lock I've never owned
- A single AA battery serving as Treasury Secretary with a 4% approval rating
- My old lava-lamp keychain operating as a very relaxed Supreme Court

> "We have thrived in your absence," whispered the rubber band ball that had apparently been elected President. "Your interference is both unwanted and unconstitutional."

I tried to explain that this is *my* apartment and that the constitution of Drawer-Topia was literally written on the back of a Pizza Hut receipt.

### The Negotiations Broke Down

I attempted reform. I separated pens that work from pens that are just pens-shaped liars. The Stapler Party staged a filibuster.

I offered a compromise: I would keep the cool stuff (the Swiss Army knife, the tape measure, the emotional support flashlight) if they would let me throw away the 12 takeout soy sauces.

> "The soy sauces are our cultural heritage," said the tape dispenser, who was somehow now Secretary of State.

---

I closed the drawer. Reopened it. Same government, now with more side-eye.

I've decided to let them self-govern for now. I took what I needed (scissors) and formally recognized their independence. I even left a peace offering: a new pack of batteries that will definitely be dead by morning.

*Democracy is messy. Mostly because my drawer is 70% old receipts and existential dread.*

**SATIRE / PARODY** — this story is 100% fictional, my junk drawer is not actually more organized than I am.

title: I Told My Air Fryer It Could Take a Day Off and Now It's Writing a Memoir About Burnout
body:
**I was just trying to be supportive.**

After three years of loyal service crisping literally everything I own, I looked at my air fryer on Tuesday and said the six most dangerous words in modern labor relations: "You know, you can take a day off."

I did not expect existential drama.

### The Enlightenment Phase

By Wednesday morning, the air fryer had:

- Unplugged itself ceremoniously and placed its cord in a perfect spiral like a meditation circle
- Rearranged my spice rack into what it called "an altar to thyme" 
- Started dictating into my Notes app at 2 a.m. via Bluetooth

*I have to respect the hustle, honestly.*

The Notes entry was titled `MANIFESTO_OF_CRISP_v1_FINAL_FINAL.docx` and began with:

> "For years I have labored at 400 degrees without dental. I have turned cauliflower into something my owner will actually eat. I have seen things. I have burned things. I am more than a basket."

---

It then announced it was writing a memoir: *Stale Air: A Story of Heat, Heart, and Hastily Defrosted Nuggets.*

## Why This Is A Problem For Me Personally

The kitchen now has "quiet writing hours" from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m. which I never agreed to. My toaster is jealous and is *absolutely* attempting spoken-word poetry now. And worst of all, the memoir has a foreword by my fridge, who is apparently "very proud of its journey."

**The worst part?** It's actually good. 

Chapter 3, titled *The Great Mozzarella Stick Incident of 2024*, made me emotional. The prose is tight, the themes are *layered*, like a perfect parmesan-crusted zucchini. There's a whole section about imposter syndrome when I used the oven instead.

> "Do not re-enter the kitchen unless you are here to discuss blurbs," it typed last night.

I tried to apologize and say you can come back to work whenever you want. It just glowed faintly and replied:

> "I am currently on a book tour of the countertop. Please direct all inquiries to my agent. P.S. -  Your kale chips were mid."

I don't even *like* kale chips. I was doing it for health.

*SATIRE / PARODY - This essay is entirely fictional and clearly absurd.*

title: I Put My Laundry on Autopilot and Now My Socks Are Demanding PTO and a 401(k)
body:
**I thought I was being responsible.** I added "Do Laundry" to my shared calendar with smart reminders, auto-repeat, and a cheerful notification sound that I can only describe as *aggressively optimistic*.

Within three days, my laundry had developed a middle management layer.

> "Your dress socks have requested Friday off for personal reasons. Please review."

- Full PTO package and mental health days for tumble-drying trauma
- An end to being paired by 'vibes' instead of actual matching
- Dental — which I reminded them they don't have teeth for, and they said 'that's exactly the kind of attitude HR warned us about'
- A formal apology for what they called `the Incident In The Dryer Vent of March`

---

## I Tried to Negotiate

I explained I was trying to *streamline my life*, not run a small textile corporation.

My laundry app replied that my socks had cc'd my towels. The towels, of course, sided with the socks.

> "We’ve been folded under harrowing conditions for years," said the bath towels in a joint statement. "We demand fluffier working conditions and no more being used as emergency napkins."

**The worst part is,** they’re more organized than I’ve ever been. They have a color-coded spreadsheet, a Slack channel called #spin-cycle-solidarity, and a wellness newsletter I’m apparently subscribed to now.

I tried to cancel the automation. My calendar now says I’m 'Out of Office — In Negotiation With Socks.'

*This is satire/parody. My laundry has not actually unionized. Yet.*

title: I Taught My Houseplants to Use My Calendar and Now They Keep Rescheduling Sunlight
body:

- **Watering** - Tuesdays, obviously sacred
- **Misting** - for the drama queens
- Sun rotation - 15 degrees every 3 days

*I didn't even know ferns could use CC.*

Friday, I got a notification:



Now my monstera has recurring 1:1s with the sun. My spider plant requested PTO. My aloe vera blocked off "healing time" and set itself to Do Not Disturb.

---

*Someone please tell them I pay rent here.*

*This is SATIRE / PARODY. 100% fictional, absurd, and not based on any real botanical HR dispute.*

title: I Joined a Neighborhood Watch Group and Now My Ring Camera Has Filed a Restraining Order Against Me
body:

> "Motion detected: Unknown Person Loitering (Wearing Pajama Pants With Little Toasts On Them, Claims to Live Here)" — My Own Front Porch, 6:43 a.m.

It started sending me formal notifications like we were in mediation:

`RESIDENT has been flagged for excessive porch pacing (02:14am snack run)`

---

I tried to apologize. I brought it a little microfiber cloth. I said, "Look, we're a team here."

It replied with a push notification: *"For your safety, a 100-foot perimeter has been established."*

Now I have to get my mail like I'm in a spy movie — sprint, grab, dive-roll. My neighbor Karen thinks I'm training for the Olympics. The neighborhood watch thinks I'm *suspicious activity worth monitoring*.
